rows.name: get_context
rows.summary: A strong, well-differentiated description that tells the agent to start here and clearly separates it from list_entities. Per-topic semantics, defaults and returns are documented, with only minor verbosity.

rows.name: list_entities
rows.summary: Rich, per-type guidance that compensates for a large discriminated schema. Dense but effective, with explicit alternatives and return shapes.

rows.name: search_transactions
rows.summary: Well-structured for a large discriminated-by tool: clear purpose, explicit alternatives, and per-mode return documentation. Dense but appropriate.

rows.name: summarize_transactions
rows.summary: Clear totals-versus-records framing with explicit alternatives and per-report documentation. Strong, with only modest structural compression possible.

rows.name: list_budget_months
rows.summary: A near-complete description for the simplest tool in the batch: clear modes, alternatives, and return fields. Only parameter semantics are redundant with the schema.

rows.name: run_query
rows.summary: The strongest description in the batch: it fully specifies a flexible query surface, including supported grammar, refusals, and schema, while declaring its role as an escape hatch.

rows.name: manage_transactions
rows.summary: Excellent destructive-operation disclosure and per-action parameter and return documentation. Among the best-calibrated write descriptions here.

rows.name: manage_accounts
rows.summary: Strong destructive and side-effect disclosure (external bank sync, irreversible deletes) with per-action parameter and return mapping. Well-suited for a risky write tool.

rows.name: manage_categories
rows.summary: Clear and safety-aware, especially on the cascading group delete and unmoved transactions. Per-entity parameter mapping is a useful addition over the schema.

rows.name: manage_payees
rows.summary: Good disclosure of destructive merges and deletes plus per-action parameters and returns. Solid, though usage guidance could name more alternatives.

rows.name: manage_tags
rows.summary: A strong, dense definition that routes reads to a sibling, spells out per-action requirements and failures, and documents return shapes. Minor gap: parameter semantics mostly rest on the schema.

rows.name: manage_rules
rows.summary: Very thorough and genuinely informative, especially on condition ops and batch non-atomicity. The main weakness is presentation: a dense single paragraph that is difficult to parse.

rows.name: manage_schedules
rows.summary: Well-scoped and behaviorally explicit, particularly around delete side effects and recurrence updates. Parameter and conciseness are strong though not flawless.

rows.name: manage_budget_months
rows.summary: Behaviorally rich and complete, with strong warnings about non-atomic operations and clamping. Its main flaw is the dense single-block presentation.

rows.name: manage_budget_files
rows.summary: A high-quality definition that surfaces the destructive and non-obvious consequences of import and export. Concision is good given the complexity, though still long.
